title: Monorail data taxonomy
description: Kinds of data (categories), whose data it is (subjects) and what it is used for (uses), with Monorail's default classification: a level for every category and a floor for every subject. The levels are defaults; an organization's own data policy may classify a category differently.

attribution.changes: Entries whose source is monorail were added by Monorail, as were common, level, why, regimes and floor on every entry, and the levels and regimes themselves.

levels.name: Restricted
levels.description: Data whose exposure would seriously harm a person or the organization, or that the law singles out: health and biometric data, government ids, card and bank numbers, credentials, the contents of private messages, pen test reports, privileged legal advice. Held by as few people and systems as the work needs.

levels.name: Confidential
levels.description: Data meant for the people who work with it, whose exposure would harm a person or the organization: most personal data, source code, financial results, contracts, vulnerability findings, who the customers are.

levels.name: Internal
levels.description: Data anyone in the organization may see, but that isn't published: working documents, the list of systems and vendors, names, job titles and work contact details of people in a work context.

levels.name: Public
levels.description: Material the organization has published, or would publish without a second thought.

regimes.name: GDPR special categories
regimes.description: Special categories of personal data under GDPR Article 9, such as health, biometric and genetic data, racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership and sexual orientation.

regimes.name: GDPR criminal offence data
regimes.description: Personal data about criminal convictions and offences, under GDPR Article 10.

regimes.name: CPRA sensitive personal information
regimes.description: Sensitive personal information as California's CCPA, amended by the CPRA, defines it, such as government ids, account credentials, precise location, the contents of messages, and health and biometric data.

regimes.name: COPPA
regimes.description: Personal information collected from children under 13, under the US Children's Online Privacy Protection Act.

regimes.name: HIPAA protected health information
regimes.description: Health information that is protected health information under US HIPAA when a covered entity or its business associate holds it.

regimes.name: PCI cardholder data
regimes.description: Payment card numbers and the cardholder data stored with them, in scope for PCI DSS.
